name: t4
description: NVIDIA Tesla T4 (TU104, Turing, sm_75) at its 1590 MHz boost clock: one Vortex core per SM; the SM is the RTX 2060's (rtx2060).

sources.SM (all core knobs): Inherited from rtx2060: TU104 uses the same Turing SM
sources.NUM_CORES: 40 SMs, 2560 CUDA cores, 320 tensor cores (NVIDIA T4 data sheet; Jia et al., Table 3.1)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS: 4 MB L2 (Jia et al., Table 3.1): 16 ways over power-of-two sets
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_DATA_RATE, PLATFORM_MEMO: 256-bit GDDR6 at 10 Gbps: 16 x16 channels at 10000 MT/s, 16 x 2 B x 10 GT/s = 320 GB/s (T4 data sheet)
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1590 MHz maximum graphics clock, the clock Jia et al. measured at (Table 3.1)
sources.EXT_RASTER_ENABLE, EXT_OM_ENABLE: Inherited on: the datacenter T4 keeps Turing's graphics pipeline for virtual workstations
sources.reference: fp32_lanes is the vendor FP32 core count (FP32 FMA lanes per chip, clock-free); dram_bandwidth_gbs the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1 and Figure 3.5: L1 hit 32, L2 hit 188, L2 miss with a TLB hit 296 cycles on the T4 (TU104)
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY, L2_MSHR_SIZE: Inherited from rtx2060 (64 each way, 32 MSHRs), which the T4's measured 188-cycle L2 hit calibrates. Little's law here: 108 cycles x 201 B/cycle (320 GB/s / 1590 MHz) / (16 x 64 B) = 21.2, within the 32
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 33 core cycles beyond the L2 link, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the T4's 296-cycle global memory latency
